annotationRationale: The essential step is converting uniform planar probability into an area ratio while checking nonoverlap and boundary coverage. Unit-cell tiling and global disk-piece counting give two useful decompositions. Circle area, square area, and decimal rounding support both routes.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate because the central task converts a uniform event into an area ratio.

review.questionCheck: Independent unit-cell analysis gives probability πd² for 0≤d≤1/2. Since the probability at 1/2 is π/4>1/2, the required radius is d=1/√(2π)≈0.3989, rounding to choice B. The supplied question and key agree, and no figure is necessary. The shared AMC 12 identification is not needed for this verification.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both useful decompositions are retained: local unit cells and global boundary disk pieces. The other supplied solutions mainly vary the numerical estimate and do not require additional routes.
review.annotationCheck: Uniform geometric probability is correctly assessed. Circle area, square area, and decimal rounding are appropriate support. Lattice-point counting is properly specific to the global counting route.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate because the central task converts a uniform event into an area ratio.

methodReviews.mathCheck: For r≤1/2, each unit cell contains four quarter-disks with disjoint interiors and total area πr². Other lattice points are at least one unit from the cell. Summing over 2020² cells gives probability πr², including boundary cells. The comparison at r=1/2 validly excludes larger radii, and solving yields 0.3989, hence 0.4.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The claimed LIVE and AoPS Solution 1 correspondence is accurate, including the AoPS radius-restriction note. The candidate supplies original prose and a fuller nonoverlap and boundary justification, correctly labeled source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The repeated grid motivates using one cell. Quarter-disks, nonoverlap, boundary cells, and the restriction on d are explained without requiring a diagram or unfamiliar theorem.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All immediate nodes are used: geometric probability supplies the area ratio, circle and square formulas supply the measures, and decimal approximation supplies the requested rounding.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The three support nodes exactly match their supplied native circle-area, square-area, and rounding topics. The central geometric-probability node has no accepted CN link.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The work uses the area components of 7.G.B.4, 3.MD.C.7, and 4.MD.A.3, along with the limited rounding scope of 5.NBT.A.4. The tiling and multiplication portions of 3.MD.C.7a/b are relevant. Fractional-side tiling in 5.NF.B.4b and formula derivations in G-GMD.A.1 are not demonstrated. No US link covers the central geometric-probability node.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The assessed/support split is accurate, and every immediate ID has a visible role. The method handles the domain, overlaps, and boundaries required by the geometric-probability definition.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The counts (N-1)² interior centers, 4(N-1) side centers, and 4 corners are exhaustive and disjoint. At r≤1/2 their contributions are whole, half, and quarter disks, with no positive-area overlap or contribution from exterior lattice points. Their weighted total is N² disks, yielding probability πr² and the same correctly rounded radius 0.4.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Supplied AoPS Solution 7 contains the claimed whole/half/quarter-disk argument. The candidate independently explains the coordinate counts and radius conditions in original prose and a justified table. The source-informed-original basis is appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The boundary-based first move is clear. Coordinate ranges justify all nontrivial table entries, the fractions follow from center location, and the displayed simplification explains why the boundary contributions combine exactly.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All five immediate IDs are supported. In particular, math:lattice-counting directly describes the interior, side, and corner coordinate counts, rather than merely referring broadly to a coordinate-plane setting.
